subject: pathology
title: Acute Tubular Necrosis, Muddy Brown Casts, Pyelonephritis, and White Cell Casts

steps.tx: Acute tubular necrosis kills tubular epithelial cells through ischaemia after shock and sepsis or toxins from aminoglycosides, contrast, myoglobin, and cisplatin, oliguria following with muddy sediment. That epithelial death is **acute tubular necrosis (ATN)**. This point is tested repeatedly because it changes everyday bedside decisions.
steps.say: Shock or toxin, then muddy urine and rising creatinine: acute tubular necrosis is AKI's workhorse.

vis.caption: Acute tubular necrosis pathophysiology from ischaemia and toxins to oliguria.

steps.tx: Muddy brown casts pack renal tubular epithelial cells and debris into granular cylinders under microscopy, sediment evidence separating ATN from prerenal azotaemia's bland hyaline casts. Those muddy cylinders are **muddy brown casts of acute tubular necrosis**. Examiners return to it because it separates careful clinicians from guesswork.
steps.say: Muddy brown casts convict tubular necrosis; bland sediment acquits toward prerenal physiology.

steps.tx: Fractional excretion of sodium below one percent favours prerenal states and above two tubular necrosis, yet diuretics, sepsis, and contrast blur it toward urea fractional excretion alternatives. That caveat discipline is **fractional excretion interpretation in AKI**. Bedside recognition of this pattern saves time, blood, and unnecessary investigation.
steps.say: FENa helps until diuretics arrive; FE urea and sediment together outvote any single number.

steps.tx: Acute pyelonephritis ascends infected urine into renal parenchyma with fever, flank pain, leucocyte casts, and neutrophil tubulitis, scarring children with reflux and obstructed adults dangerously. That ascending infection is **acute pyelonephritis**. Students should anchor this fact before moving to rarer causes and exceptions.
steps.say: Fever, flank pain, and white cell casts localise urinary infection into kidney parenchyma itself.

vis.caption: Acute pyelonephritis renal pathology with neutrophilic tubulointerstitial inflammation.

steps.tx: White cell casts form when leucocytes pack tubular lumens in pyelonephritis or interstitial nephritis, urinary proof that white cells originate inside kidney rather than bladder below. Those cylinders are **white cell (leucocyte) casts of renal inflammation**. In practice this distinction decides the next test, treatment, or referral made.
steps.say: White cells cast in tubules prove kidney level inflammation; bladder infection cannot manufacture casts.

steps.tx: Chronic pyelonephritis scars calyces and overlying parenchyma coarsely from reflux or obstruction, thyroidisation tubules dilating with colloid like casts in end stage patterns. That coarse scarring is **chronic pyelonephritis of reflux and obstruction**. That is why this detail earns its place in every examination and ward round.
steps.say: Calyceal clubbing with overlying scars means chronic pyelonephritis; find reflux or obstruction behind it.

vis.caption: Tubulointerstitial and pyelonephritis spectrum toward chronic scarring.

steps.tx: Acute interstitial nephritis inflames interstitium immunologically after beta lactams, proton pump inhibitors, NSAIDs, or checkpoint inhibitors, AKI with sterile pyuria, biopsy guiding steroid debates. Drug timing solves **acute interstitial nephritis (AIN)**. Remembering it prevents the commonest errors made with this presentation entirely.
steps.say: New drug, rising creatinine, sterile pyuria: interstitial nephritis until the medication chart is acquitted.

rows: White cells and white cell casts

steps.tx: Obstruction injures tubules by back pressure at any level from prostate to retroperitoneal fibrosis, ultrasound hydronephrosis and post relief diuresis charting its course and urgency. That reversible cause is **obstructive acute kidney injury**. The clinical payoff comes from applying it early, before complications accumulate further.
steps.say: Every AKI earns a bladder scan and obstruction thought; relief timing decides recovered function.
